key_insight: VIME combines classical imaginary-time pre-training with a compressed ansatz to generate much cheaper ground-state preparation circuits while preserving high energy accuracy.
engineering_relevance: The method directly targets early fault-tolerant quantum chemistry by reducing qubit, CNOT, and circuit-depth demands for preparing molecular ground states.
method: Extends operator-projected variational imaginary-time evolution to molecular electronic structure using a single compiled Majorana-propagation surrogate graph.
Pairs this with a compressed tiled Unitary Product State (c-tUPS) ansatz to lower both classical simulation cost and quantum state-preparation cost.
Uses classical pre-training to produce hardware-efficient circuit structures before deployment on quantum devices.
evidence_signal: On TLD-1411, active-space calculations up to 52 qubits reached chemical precision versus DMRG with energy errors about 400× smaller than ADAPT-VQE-based VMPE, and across acenes up to heptacene (60 qubits) VIME matched or improved accuracy with up to 26× fewer CNOTs and 167× lower two-qubit depth.
watch_item: Results depend on active-space selection and pre-training quality, so performance may vary for molecules where the surrogate Majorana graph or compressed ansatz is less expressive.
paper_title: Hardware-Efficient Ground-State Preparation using Variational Imaginary-Time Majorana Evolution
